title: Tiered audit storage: ingestion pipeline overhaul, time/tenant partitioning, and cost-aware retention
creator: Maya Chen
description: Replace the current monolithic audit ingest+indexing flow with a tiered hot/warm/cold storage architecture and tenant-aware partitioning. Goals: (1) reduce long-term storage costs while preserving query performance for recent/important events, (2) provide predictable per-tenant cost allocation and retention policy controls, (3) make ingestion resilient to spikes and idempotent for retries, and (4) instrument retention decisions for legal/compliance requests. Work touches ingest pipeline (Kafka topics, dedupe, schema), index layout (time + tenant shards), compaction/eviction policies, cold-store lifecycle, and console cost dashboards.
acceptance_criteria: New ingestion pipeline writes events to hot topic and tags tenant+region metadata; end-to-end latency <= 2s for hot writes under typical load
Indexes are time-partitioned (daily) with optional hashed tenant sub-partitioning; query latency for last 7 days comparable to baseline
Cold tier lifecycle moves data to object store with manifest-based index snapshots; cost reduction >= 35% for 12-month retention compared to current indices
Retention policy service supports per-tenant overrides and legal-hold flags; console exposes retention and cost breakdown per tenant
Migration plan and backfill tested in staging with sample of 1000 tenants; no data loss during cutover; migration playbook documented in Confluence
Alerting and SLIs: lost-events rate < 0.01% after rollout; indexing backlog processed within configured window
work_items: Design: time+tenant partitioning scheme and shard sizing model
Ingest: introduce dedupe key, idempotent writes, and hot-topic sharding by tenant hash
Indexing: implement daily partitions + hashed tenant buckets; add index manifest format for cold snapshots
Cold tier: implement S3/GCS lifecycle export, compacted index snapshots, and restore path
Retention service: policy engine with per-tenant rules, legal-hold checks, and safe-delete workflow
Cost tooling: offline simulator to estimate storage + query cost by retention window; integrate into Console
Migration: build backfill tooling and phased cutover plan with canary tenants
Observability: add per-tenant cost metrics, indexing backlog gauge, and retention action audit events
progress_updates: 2026-02-18: Design review complete. Decided on daily time partitions + 256 tenant buckets per shard; pros/cons documented (see Confluence).
2026-02-25: PoC ingest changes merged to feature branch: writes include dedupe_id and tenant_hash; local staging shows idempotent retries work as expected.
2026-03-03: Index manifest schema v1 proposed; reviewed by infra and storage teams. Requires small change to existing restore path (commented in PR #4821).
2026-03-09: Cost simulator spike test: with current traffic distribution, moving 90 days->cold after 7 days yields ~40% storage savings and 8% increase in cold-read latency for archived queries.
2026-03-12: Kickoff for migration staging run scheduled; blocked on S3 lifecycle role and KMS grant for cold-store (see blockers).
blockers: KMS grants for write/restore operations to customer-managed key in cold bucket
Production quota for additional Kafka partitions during canary run
Legal-team confirmation on default tenant retention bounds and legal-hold API contract
notes: Trade-offs considered: larger tenant buckets reduce metadata overhead but risk noisy-tenant hotspots; chosen 256 buckets based on current tenant cardinality and read/write QPS distribution.
Alternative cold-store approach (keep inverted indices in object store) rejected due to restore complexity and query-time compaction cost.
Migration plan will run in phases: (1) internal-only tenants canary, (2) low-throughput external tenants, (3) full migration. Rollback path includes replay from retained hot-topic window.
